note: Hand-curated. Every entry needs a source URL from a news outlet before it ships — scripts/suggest_openings.py surfaces candidates and the Brief's archive (btownbrief/archive stories.json openClose tags) is the deep well; a human verifies and adds them here. Dates we could not pin to a day carry a 'reported' label.

entries.name: Homeport at the Essex Experience
entries.dateLabel: soft opened July · grand opening August 1, 2026
entries.story: The Church Street housewares mainstay opened a second, 6,000-square-foot store at the Essex Experience — kitchen goods and housewares, timed to the flagship's 20th anniversary.

entries.name: Old Brick Store outpost (Public Service VT)
entries.area: Karma Bird House, Maple St, Burlington
entries.story: The team behind Charlotte's beloved Old Brick Store takes over the Kestrel Coffee café space at Karma Bird House — pastries, espresso, and prepared food, "the Brick on a small scale."

entries.name: Wild Meadows Books & Café
entries.dateLabel: opened early July 2026 · grand opening July 11–12
entries.story: The Williston Observer's owners opened the town's only general-interest bookstore, with local art on the walls and Mirabelles treats at the café counter.

entries.name: Nostalgia Toys & More
entries.story: The retro toy shop lasted seven months in the corner storefront that was Weenies Hot Dogs — rent, staffing, and theft made it unsustainable, the owners said.

entries.name: Feldman's Bagels
entries.story: The South End bagel shop went out of business overnight — customers found a handwritten sign on the door; the St. Albans location closed the same day.

entries.name: Burl's Downtown Kitchenette
entries.story: The Farmhouse Group turned the 1954 Oasis diner car into an all-day Southern-leaning diner — biscuits and gravy, fried chicken and waffles, patty melts, a full bar.

entries.name: The Harborvale
entries.story: The former Courtyard by Marriott reopened as a 161-room Autograph Collection hotel from the Hotel Vermont team, with chef Doug Paine's Lake Champlain-focused restaurant.

entries.name: El Cortijo Taqueria
entries.story: After 15 years the Farmhouse Group's taqueria served its last tacos in the Bank Street diner car, making way for Burl's Downtown Kitchenette.

entries.name: El Gato Cantina (Essex Junction)
entries.area: Park St at Five Corners, Essex Junction
entries.story: After a dozen years at the Five Corners, the Mexican restaurant closed ahead of the building's planned demolition — it's hunting a new Essex-area home, and the Jeffersonville and Smugglers' Notch spots carry on.

entries.name: J.Crew
entries.story: The national clothing brand filled a former Mexican-restaurant space at Maple Tree Place — one of several big names landing in Williston's shopping hub this year.

entries.name: PopUp Bagels
entries.dateLabel: announced May 2026 · no opening date yet
entries.story: The fast-growing chain known for bagel-and-schmear combos with rotating specialty cream cheeses picked the Marketplace storefront Black Cap Coffee left behind for its first Vermont outpost.

entries.name: Small Dog Electronics (retail store)
entries.story: The region's only approved Apple repair-and-resell shop closed its Burlington storefront and moved the business online.

entries.name: Kestrel Coffee Roasters (Pine St)
entries.story: The Pine Street café poured its last shots mid-April — "all good things evolve," the owners said; their other locations stayed open.

entries.name: Café Napoli
entries.dateLabel: announced · was aiming for late March 2026 — opening unconfirmed
entries.story: After a decade pulling shots at the Cosmic Grind, barista Cole Thornton opened his own espresso bar with partner Dante Seguino in the cozy space that once housed Lucky Next Door.

entries.name: Savu Sauna bathhouse
entries.story: The outdoor-sauna company that's been steaming lakeside since 2021 is building an 8,000-square-foot bathhouse — multiple saunas, a steam room, warm pools, and a cold plunge.

entries.name: Thai in the Alley
entries.story: The alley spot behind the Marketplace is back in business, replacing BKK in the Alley — the Stowe Thai Cuisine owner and chef Tokyo Asissara serve a menu that roams Thailand's regions.

entries.name: Mothership Brewery
entries.story: The brewpub at American Flatbread — the very room where Zero Gravity was born in 2004 — relaunched as Mothership Brewery under head brewer Destiny Saxon, taps pouring only at the Hearth.

entries.name: Drink
entries.area: St. Paul St at City Hall Park, Burlington
entries.story: The low-key cocktail bar across from City Hall Park — born in 1999 as Wine Works and rebranded a few times since — called it after more than a quarter century of trivia, comedy, and live music.

entries.name: Pascolo Ristorante
entries.story: The Italian spot moved back into its original subterranean home at 83 Church Street after three years up the block — same menu, same staff.

entries.name: Mountain Valley Indian Cuisine
entries.story: The couple behind Winooski's Mountain Valley Restaurant brought their tandoori, curries, and hand-pleated momos to a former Domino's on Farrell Street.

entries.name: Dear Lucy
entries.story: The longtime Church Street shoe store closed its doors, its owner saying retail — and downtown — had changed.

entries.name: Black Cap Coffee & Bakery (Church St)
entries.story: Two years of sliding sales ended the Church Street café's run days after its baristas walked out; the non-union Stowe, Morrisville, and Waterbury shops carry on.

entries.name: Scale Poké Bar
entries.story: The poké chain's third Vermont location landed in South Burlington's City Center neighborhood.

entries.name: Partizanfilm
entries.story: A member-run nonprofit micro-cinema filled the void the Roxy left — two intimate screening rooms (31 and 19 seats) and a café-bookstore lobby, programmed seven days a week.

entries.name: The Chocolate Butcher Chop Shop
entries.story: Rough-cut chocolate chunks, truffles, and snack boards, sold butcher-style in Williston.

entries.name: Citizen Cider Press House Pub
entries.story: After permitting delays pushed it months past target, the cidery consolidated under one roof on Flynn Avenue — indoor food-truck kitchen, smash burgers, and the full tap list.

entries.name: Burlington Square (AC Hotel by Marriott)
entries.story: A decade after the mall came down, "the Pit" became Burlington Square — a 161-room AC Hotel, 53 apartments, and street-level food, with a second tower still to come.

entries.name: The Gryphon
entries.story: The Main Street gastropub closed after 11 years, citing a "trying last year" of construction detours and downtown struggles — weeks after Nectar's went dark up the street.

entries.name: La Di Da Pizza
entries.story: New York native Celine Eid turned the former Despacito space into a NYC-style slice shop, with seasonal pies and grab-and-go energy in the Old North End.

entries.name: Riko's Pizza
entries.story: The Connecticut tavern-style pizza chain opened with fanfare in late January and was gone by mid-August — the franchisee said the location didn't fit the brand's growth plans.

entries.name: Nectar's
entries.story: The club that gave Phish its start played its final set after nearly 50 years — construction, changing nightlife, and failed lease talks finally ended a Burlington institution.

entries.name: Playa Bowls
entries.story: The açaí-bowl chain's first Vermont location joined the Dorset Street food rush.

entries.name: Wings Over Burlington
entries.story: The wing shop returned to Dorset Street under corporate ownership, four months after the franchise abruptly closed.

entries.name: Half Pint Pizza
entries.story: The Daily Planet team set up a permanent pizza kitchen inside their friends' brewery — a symbiotic South Burlington pairing that gives beer drinkers a reason to stay.

entries.name: The District VT (formerly ArtsRiot)
entries.dateLabel: closed late May 2025 · weeks after rebrand
entries.story: The Pine Street venue shut its doors "effective immediately" just weeks after shedding the ArtsRiot name, capping years of ownership churn — all upcoming shows canceled.

entries.name: The Mad Taco (Shelburne Rd)
entries.story: The Vermont taco mini-chain rolled its fifth location — a food truck parked at the new Gardener's Supply — so plant shopping and taco feasting now go hand in hand.

entries.name: PayMore
entries.story: The electronics buyback shop gives that drawer of tangled chargers and retro consoles a second life — recycling, but with cash back.

entries.name: Firehouse Subs
entries.story: The national sandwich chain's first-ever Vermont restaurant opened in Williston, with a slice of each sale going to public-safety groups.

entries.name: Manhattan's (Manhattan Pizza & Pub)
entries.story: The late-night pizza-and-music corner was shut by the fire marshal over unpermitted work weeks after reopening as Manhattan's — it never came back, and What Ales You later claimed the space.
